from.place: proof, finite duality identifies the right adjoint for a finite morphism and describes the counit

title: Finite Grothendieck duality as derived Hom with counit evaluation
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $K$ be an object of $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] (bounded below with quasi-coherent cohomology). Let $f^!K$ denote the right adjoint image for $Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$, compatible with the $f_*\mathcal O_X$-module structure, $Rf_*f^!K\simeq R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,K)$. Under this canonical isomorphism, the adjunction counit $Rf_*f^!K\to K$ is induced by evaluation at the unit section $1\in f_*\mathcal O_X$.

proof.text: Because $f$ is finite between Noetherian schemes, the finite pseudo-coherence and internal-Hom quasi-coherence argument gives $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,K)\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)$, and hence its image lies in $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$, exactly as stated in [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-derived-hom-qcoherent].

source.place: Tag 0AX2, lemma-finite-twisted: pseudo-coherence and quasi-coherence paragraphs

proof.text: The finite morphism is affine, and $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ has a right adjoint $f^!$ by [lem-pc-noetherian-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint] ($X,Y$ Noetherian). By [lem-sc-finite-affine-derived-equivalence], $Rf_*$ induces an equivalence $\Phi:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)$ whose composition with restriction is $Rf_*$; hence $\Phi\circ f^!$ is right adjoint to restriction $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$, with the counit of $Rf_*\dashv f^!$ as counit. By [lem-sc-finite-twisted-inverse-bounded-below], $f^!K\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)$, so $\Phi f^!K\in D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)$. By [lem-sc-finite-sheafhom-affine-adjoint], $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,-)$ is right adjoint to restriction, with counit evaluation at $1$, and by Step 1 it sends $K$ into $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)$. Hence, restricting both adjunctions to the full subcategories $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, uniqueness of right adjoints gives a canonical isomorphism $\Phi f^!K\simeq R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,K)$ in $D^+_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(f_*\mathcal O_X)$ carrying the counit of $Rf_*\dashv f^!$ to the evaluation counit. The uniqueness argument is elementary: two right adjoints to the same functor are uniquely isomorphic by composing one unit with the other counit, and the resulting isomorphism is the unique one preserving counits.

source.place: Tag 0AX2, lemma-finite-twisted: lemma-sheafhom-affine-adjoint, lemma-twisted-inverse-image-bounded-below, and comparison of right adjoints

proof.text: Applying the restriction (forgetful) functor from $D(f_*\mathcal O_X)$ to $D(\mathcal O_Y)$, which sends $\Phi f^!K$ to $Rf_*f^!K$, preserves this canonical comparison and its counit. Therefore the displayed isomorphism $Rf_*f^!K\simeq R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(f_*\mathcal O_X,K)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y)$ is compatible with the $f_*\mathcal O_X$-module structure, and its counit is evaluation at $1\in f_*\mathcal O_X$ by the counit clause of [lem-sc-finite-sheafhom-affine-adjoint].
